subject: Post-call: Acme integration & model-routing next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call: Acme integration & model-routing next steps

Thanks for the time earlier today — great discussion. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Goal: integrate Redwood’s runtime for Acme’s customer support assistant (chat) + semantic search (knowledge base) + a light reranker for response quality.
- Integration surface: frontend chat -> Redwood API (chat + tool-calling for ticket lookups) and backend embeddings pipeline for KB search + reranker.
- Auth: we'll support server-side API keys for backend and short-lived/ephemeral tokens for browser flows (we recommend a proxy pattern).
- Model-routing requirements: low-latency primary for chat (~<200ms p50), embedding throughput for nightly indexing, reranker only in top-k re-rank path. Need cost budget guidance from you.
- Policy/fallback: propose primary model for chat (redwood-chat-4k) with fallback to a smaller variant (redwood-chat-2k-eco) on cost/latency triggers; embeddings use redwood-embed-1; reranker is a supervised ranker model.

Attached: high-level architecture diagram (acme-integration-arch.png). Action items:
1) Sasha: share a staging account and sample KB (CSV or docs) so we can size embedding pipeline.
2) Kevin: confirm procurement timeline; we can provide an estimate for Dedicated or Hosted pricing.
3) Dev: follow up with SDK/auth examples and model-routing policy draft.

I'll loop Marcus from infra for the specific routing policy thresholds. Let us know availability for a 30-min technical deep-dive this week.

Regards,

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Acme integration & model-routing next steps — SDK + auth + routing draft

Hi Sasha — copying the technical details below and attaching an SDK quickstart (sdk-setup.md) and a draft policy YAML (model-routing-policy.yaml). TL;DR: server keys for backend, ephemeral JWTs for browser flows via short-lived mint endpoint; embed pipeline should be incremental with batched upserts.

Auth (recommended):
- Backend jobs / ingestion: use a static API key scoped to the ingestion project. Rotate keys quarterly.
- Frontend chat: mint ephemeral tokens (1-5 minute TTL) from your backend. Tokens are scoped to a session id and can be revoked via session blacklist in the backend. Redwood supports a token revocation endpoint in Private/Dedicated; for Hosted we provide short TTLs and session revocation hooks.

SDK example (Node, simplified):
const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/inference-sdk');
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
const chat = await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-chat-4k', input: '...', session_id: 'sess-123' });

For browser flows, call your backend: POST /mint-token -> returns ephemeral token for the client. Client uses token for chat calls to Redwood.

Model routing & policy (high-level):
- Route by policy: 
  - latency_slo_ms: 200 (p50) -> prefer redwood-chat-4k in us-west region.
  - cost_threshold_per_1k_tokens_usd: 0.80 -> if expected cost > threshold, route to eco model redwood-chat-2k-eco.
  - fallback_chain: [redwood-chat-4k, redwood-chat-2k-eco, redwood-chat-1b-fallback] for degraded infra.
  - region_preference: [us-west, us-east] with auto-failover.

Embeddings pipe: incremental upserts via batch API (we recommend chunk size 512 docs per batch for your KB size). Storage: estimate ~768MB per 1M vectors at 1536-d float16 — you should be well within budget for 250k docs. We can provide more precise numbers with a sample extract.

Reranker integration:
- Query: semantic search -> top-50 candidates -> lightweight reranker on top-10.
- Latency guidance: aim for reranker sub-100ms added latency for the top-10 when colocated in us-west dedicated pool; on Hosted expect ~150-250ms depending on model.

Attached: sdk-setup.md (quickstart), model-routing-policy.yaml (example policy you can tweak). Happy to jump on a 30-min deep-dive to walk through the YAML and SDK flows.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: Acme integration & model-routing next steps — routing policy thresholds

Adding infra specifics / proposal on thresholds: 

Proposal:
- Primary chat model: redwood-chat-4k (colocated in us-west).
- Cost/latency policy: p50_latency_target_ms = 200, p95_latency_target_ms = 400. If p50 > 200ms for 2 consecutive minutes or queue depth > 30, trigger route to eco model.
- Cost budget enforcement: compute estimated cost per 1k tokens in realtime using token estimator in the routing layer. If 1k-token cost > $0.80, route to eco model for that request.
- Fallback chain behavior: when region unavailable, automatically failover to us-east; if both are constrained, degrade response length and use redwood-chat-1b-fallback.

Operational notes:
- We'll expose per-route metrics in the Console so your SREs can set alerts (latency, error-rate, fallback-rate).
- For reranker: run on a dedicated small pool to keep p95 < 250ms; batch top-k scoring when traffic allows.

Next steps: we can prototype the routing policy in your staging project for 1 week and produce a short report on latency/cost tradeoffs. ETA for prototype: 7 business days after staging access is provided.

—Marcus
